notes: The booklet pictures are small and low-resolution. Piece-to-piece attachments are my best reading, so some pieces may be attached to a neighbouring piece rather than the exact one shown. This applies most to the car body (3710 plates, 3665 slopes, 3666 plates, 54200 slopes) and the trailer floor (red 3008/3665/3063b and black plates).
Quantities and colours match the parts list exactly: 168 pieces. The 3 repeat groups of wheel holder, wheel and tyre account for 24 of them.
The two minifigures (head, hair, torso, legs) are not in the parts list, so they are not modelled.

The brown 1x2 brick and tile (b2, b3) sit on the horse in step 2 and are removed again before the saddle goes on. I kept them joined to each other and added a contact edge to the horse for where they rest.
Per the picture, each of the 8 wheel holders carries one wheel with its tyre. The car has 4 holders and the trailer has 4.
The sticker sheet (b87) is joined to the car side bricks, the rear licence plate and the trailer tiles as a nominal sticker attachment.
The trailer drawbar towball (b94) is joined to the car hitch socket (b12), as in the final picture. The tailgate is hinged to the trailer rear clips through the 1x2 handle plates (b139, b140).
The parts list has no drawbar triangle, so lego-2508 (black long towball plate) stands in for the black drawbar piece.

The remaining 2 disconnected groups are real. The booklet's own overview (page 2) shows the pieces as separate models: bag 1 makes the 4WD, horse and saddle, and bag 2 makes the trailer and fence. The vehicle with trailer is one group. The horse, brown brick/tile, saddle and fence are the other. The saddle only rests on the fence in the final picture. Nothing physically connects the horse or fence to the vehicle, so I did not add an edge that the manual does not show.
